thread:
lucas: Ran an nsys capture on the long-tail latency regression — timeline shows repeated host->device memcpy bursts on a dedicated copy stream that line up with big GPU kernels on the compute stream, causing serialization and tail spikes. attaching notes.

infra-bot: nsys upload complete: s3://redwood-nsys/regress-1766004321 (uploaded by infra-bot) :white_check_mark:

maya: Can you paste the small timeline snippet or NVTX ranges? guessing this is stream priority / memcpy scheduling.

lucas: Here's the command I ran and the quick TL;DR from the UI:
```
nsys profile --trace=cuda,osrt,nvtx --output=regress-1766004321 ./run_infer.sh

# timeline notes (from nsys ui)
stream 11 (copy): host->device memcpy x 10, ~0.8-1.6ms each
stream 0 (compute): large DecoderLayer kernels often start slightly after copy ops but stall waiting on PCIe
CPU: submit thread shows repeated pthread_yield / scheduling gaps ~400-700us
```

jia: Those copy bursts — are they KV cache prefetch or something else?

lucas: Looks like KV prefetch on cold requests. We prefetch full KV per micro-batch; many small async memcpys get queued on a copy stream. The driver sometimes executes the memcpy bursts ahead of the compute stream (or blocks kernels) leading to effective serialization and tail latency.

noah: Do we set explicit priorities for compute vs copy streams? I thought compute had higher priority and copies lower, but driver behavior can be surprising if streams are created without priority or if priority ranges overlap.

maya: There was a recent change that created copy streams without a priority arg (defaults). If copies end up on equal priority to compute, scheduling can interleave in a way that hurts us. Also check whether the copy stream uses non-blocking vs blocking memcpy.

lucas: Repro command for a tiny case I used:
```
CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=0 nsys profile --trace=cuda,nvtx --output=mini ./mini_kv_prefetch.sh
```
Mini timeline shows 8 successive H2D async copies finishing ~in the same 5ms window, then a big compute kernel that waits for them.

jia: Two ideas: (A) create the copy stream with lower priority than compute (cudaStreamCreateWithPriority), or (B) merge multiple small prefetches into one larger memcpy to reduce PCIe chatter. B reduces number of DMA transactions and chances for interleaving.

noah: Also look at CPU side: the submitter thread is getting preempted (I can see SCHED preempt markers). If submitter is scheduled late, a backlog of memcpy launches happens at once and the copy engine gets overwhelmed. Consider pinning the submit thread or raising its niceness.

lucas: Good call — our prefetch runs on a threadpool. Under load the pool threads get preempted and then wake and flood-copy. I'll try (1) forcing copy streams to low priority, (2) a quick prefetch-merge heuristic, and (3) adding NVTX ranges to mark KV-prefetch for better correlation.

maya: For triage, also add a counter metric: memcpy_count_per_request and avg_memcpy_size. That will tell us whether it's many small copies.

lucas: Quick patch plan:
1) create copy stream via cudaStreamCreateWithPriority(low_priority)
2) coalesce contiguous KV pages into page-aligned larger transfers when possible
3) pin submitter thread to a CPU core and set sched nice for io threads
I'll run another nsys capture after each change. ETA ~2h.

infra-bot: deploy-robot: branch lucas/low-prio-copy-stream pushed, CI build queued.

jia: If that fixes most tails, we should follow-up in batching heuristics: avoid full-KV fetch for tiny micro-batches (<8 tokens) and instead use on-demand micro-fetch.

noah: Also double-check whether the copy engine is using the copy engine or falling back to synchronous path because of pinned vs pageable buffers. Prefer pinned host buffers to get true async DMA.

lucas: Yep — will audit buffer pinning. For now I'm re-running with low-prio copy stream + pinned buffers + merged prefetch. Posting nsys TL when done.

maya: Thanks — please include the nsys call + exported JSON snippet (callstack / CUDA API events) so we can filter by stream id.

lucas: Will do. If the low-prio stream + merged prefetch reduces memcpy count by >70% we can fold into next patch and add a telemetry alert for memcpy_count spikes.

deploy-robot: CI build passed for lucas/low-prio-copy-stream. Test runs scheduled.

lucas: Re-ran capture (will upload). Early look: memcpy_count down from ~10->3 for the sample client, tail p95 latency dropped ~18%. Posting full nsys link in 30m.
